purpose: Select the fastest lawful, structurally complete Sanskrit Devimahatmya transcription candidate without acquiring or accepting a new licence.

index_observation.title: मार्कण्डेयपुराणम्
index_observation.boundary: Revision 415411 is a table-of-contents/index page, not the complete Devimahatmya text carrier.

structure.chapter_86_note: A parser that disallows whitespace after the full stop falsely reports marker 6 as absent. The fixed Wikisource text contains the stanza and literal marker with one space.
structure.structural_crosswalk: The thirteen chapter terminal counts match the retained private GRETIL 81-93 witness after recognizing the chapter-86 spaced marker. This proves a structural crosswalk, not line-by-line textual identity or an identified common print source.

decision.reason: It is a compact Devanagari transcription with a complete 81-93 chapter/marker sequence and an explicit open-license lane, while the acquired alternatives are noncommercial, partial, scope-mismatched, image-only, or unsuitable as product text.
decision.next_if_authorized: Acquire the three exact revision payloads plus revision metadata into the content-addressed vault, preserve CC BY-SA attribution/share-alike obligations, segment all 13 chapters and verses, compare against the GRETIL witness and fixed scans, then produce separately attributable Hindi and English Devam translations.

held_alternatives: GRETIL Markandeyapurana 81-93: structurally complete but CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 private evidence only
Poley 1831 Sanskrit/Latin edition: complete but fixed scan restricts use to personal noncommercial purposes
Bhuti 1901 Bengali translation: explicitly volume 1 and incomplete as a standalone lane
Durgasaptashatipradipa 1919: ritual-commentary/manual scope mismatch, not the complete main text
Commons Malayalam-script palm-leaf manuscript: valuable public-domain manuscript witness, not the fastest searchable Devanagari product text
